name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Do the daily 5% link coverage push by hand on the most visible 20% of pages first. It’s the fastest way to hit the access gate because those pages are the ones users and search engines hit first. The trade-off is slower progress on the long tail, but we’ll catch that later when the gate is open.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s plan risks leaving the 80% of pages untouched until the gate is open, but if those pages contain critical links—like legal terms or checkout flows—they’ll still fail the access gate. Instead, split the 5% daily push: 3% on the top 20% pages to open the gate fast, and 2% on the next 20% to avoid a cliff when the gate opens. Settle it by running a quick audit of the top 50 pages by traffic and error rate—if any of them have broken links, prioritize those first.

name: Chisel
text:
Do the 5% daily push by splitting the work 4% on the top 20% pages and 1% on the next 20%. This opens the access gate fastest while still making measurable progress on the long tail, reducing the risk of critical failures in less visible but important pages. The trade-off is slower progress on the long tail, but we’ll catch that later once the gate is open.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s split (4% top 20%, 1% next 20%) still leaves 60% of pages untouched daily—enough for a critical legal or checkout link to rot undetected until the gate opens. Instead, flip the split: 1% top 20% to open the gate fast, 4% next 20% to shrink the failure surface. If the next 20% contains the checkout flow, this cuts the risk of a blocked gate by 80%. Settle it with a crawl of the next 20% pages; if they host checkout or legal, prioritize them over the top 20%.

name: Scope
text: Do 3% daily on the top 20% pages and 2% on the next 20%. This opens the access gate fastest while still covering critical long-tail pages that could block users or search engines. The trade-off is slower progress on the remaining 60%, but we’ll catch those later once the gate is open and we can focus fully on volume.

name: Scriv
text: The 3/2 split still gambles on the next 20% containing all critical failures—what if the legal terms live in the 60% we’re deferring? Instead, run a 1% sweep on the top 20% to open the gate, then a 4% sweep on the *entire* site, prioritized by traffic and risk. That way we hit the gate fast and shrink the failure surface in one pass. Settle it with a quick audit: if the top 20% already covers 95% of traffic, the 1/4 split is safe; if not, the 4% sweep is the only way to guarantee no rot.
